newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Wheat Pool sees little crop quality change.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Wheat Pool sees little crop quality change.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool said Friday it saw "very little" change in crop quality from the previous week except for canola where estimates for the top grade were increased.

Eighty-five percent of the canola crop was expected to grade No1 Canada, up from 72 percent last week, 12 percent should grade No2 C, down from 17 percent last week and two percent should grade No3 C, down from seven percent.
About 30 percent of hard red spring wheat should grade No1 Canada Western Red Spring, up from 29 percent last week, 10 percent should grade No2, down from 24 percent last week.
Thirty-six percent should grade as No3 CWRS, up from 30 percent last week and 24 percent should grade as feed wheat, up from 16 percent last week, AWP said.

Sixteen percent of the barley crop should grade as malt, up from 13 percent last week, 70 percent should grade as No1 Canada Western, down from 71 last week and 14 percent should grade as No2 CW, down from 16 percent last week.
